title: Synthetic production release gate field report
summary: A deliberately fictional report showing how mixed evidence can be recorded without representing a real organization, customer, or deployment.

context.setting: A fictional software-delivery team replaces an informal production release sequence with a reviewed, versioned plan and an explicit authorization gate.
constraints: The scenario is synthetic and is not derived from an employer or customer system.
The release must remain reversible and preserve a human stop decision.

method.description: The fictional team records the intended change, saves the exact infrastructure plan, verifies provenance at apply time, and requires a named human authorization before production execution.
pattern_elements: Preserve intent in the reviewed commit and saved plan.
Treat the release decision and its evidence as versioned artifacts.

signals.name: Stale-plan execution
signals.baseline: The fictional baseline allowed a plan to be recreated during release.
signals.observed: The designed gate rejects a plan when its commit, artifact digest, or state serial no longer matches.
signals.source: Synthetic walkthrough against the documented release controls

signals.name: Routine release effort
signals.baseline: The fictional baseline used one manual approval step.
signals.observed: The designed gate adds provenance checks whose operational burden has not been measured in a real release.
signals.source: Synthetic design review; no production timing data

limitations: No real user, organization, repository, or production environment was observed.
The example demonstrates the contract and cannot support pattern maturity.
No longitudinal outcome or independent replication exists.

independence.statement: This report was authored solely as a fictional schema example and is not independent evidence.
